rendered: After sulfur infiltration, the D peak red-shifts by 17 cm^−1[1]. The discharged electrode, compared with an as-prepared electrode, shows a further redshift of the D peak of 12[2] cm^-1 relative to the as-prepared electrode, not relative to the infiltrated material. The paper states a final red shift of the D peak of >25 wavenumbers[3], which it attributes to the combination of sulfur infiltration and sodiation inside the carbon.
